title: Pool Bank Shots for Beginners: Aim, Speed and the Diamond System
description: Learn how bank shots work in pool: the angle-in, angle-out idea, how to use the table diamonds, and a simple drill to start making banks.
body:
Every pool room has that one player who sinks a ball off the rail like it is no big deal, and everyone nearby goes quiet for a second. The good news: bank shots look like magic, but they follow simple geometry you can learn in an afternoon. Here is a beginner-friendly guide to banking balls with confidence.

What is a bank shot?

A bank shot is when you send the object ball into one or more cushions (rails) first, then it rolls into a pocket. Instead of aiming straight at the pocket, you aim at a spot on the rail and let the cushion redirect the ball.

Players reach for banks when a ball is blocked by other balls, when the straight-in angle is awkward, or when a bank is simply the highest-percentage option. Pros use them constantly, and fans love them: bank-shot highlights from legends like Efren Reyes are some of the most-watched pool clips around.

The big idea: angle in, angle out

Picture a ball rolling smoothly into a cushion. It leaves at roughly the same angle it arrived, like a mirror reflecting light. That is the heart of the "mirror" idea, and the popular diamond system is built on it.

A real table is not a perfect mirror, though. Speed, spin, cloth and cushion condition all change the bounce. So think of the geometry as your starting guess, not a guarantee.

Using the diamonds as your map

Those little markers on the rails are not decoration. They are aiming references. The basic recipe:

  • Find your line. Imagine a straight line from the object ball, through the rail spot where it should bounce, to the pocket.
  • Use the mirror picture. A trick many players like is to imagine the table is doubled: the pocket you want is "reflected" on the other side of the rail, and you aim straight at that reflection.
  • Aim at the spot, not the marker. Instructors point out that you should aim where the line meets the cushion edge, not at the diamond itself.
  • Check the result. Where the ball actually hits tells you how your table behaves. Adjust a little and try again.

Speed and spin change everything

This is where beginners get surprised. The same bank can land in different places depending on how you hit it:

  • Medium, steady speed is the best place to start. Very soft banks can wander, and very hard ones tend to bounce unpredictably.
  • Sidespin (English) on the cue ball can nudge the object ball slightly and change how it comes off the cushion. Many players start with no sidespin at all so there is one fewer thing to guess.
  • Table conditions matter. New cloth, old cloth, tight pockets and different cushion rubber all play differently, and tables are not all the same. Spend a few minutes testing before a match.

Want a refresher on how spin works? Our spin guide covers follow, draw and English in plain language.

A simple practice routine

  1. Pick one pocket. Put a ball on the same spot every time and bank it to the same corner.
  2. Keep your speed the same. Change only one thing per attempt: either the aim point or the speed, never both.
  3. Move the ball. After a few made banks, shift the ball a diamond over and see how the aim changes.
  4. Play a bank-only game. A common drill is a game where every ball has to be banked. It teaches you how your table plays very fast.

Keep your stroke smooth and stay down on the shot. If your fundamentals are shaky, brush up with our pre-shot routine guide first, because bank shots punish a wobbly stroke.

When to bank, and when not to

A bank is not always the smart choice. If you have a straight-in shot that you make most of the time, take it. Bank shots have less room for error, and a miss can leave your opponent an open table. When in doubt, think about the option that leaves you the best next shot, a topic we cover in our safety play guide.

Watch the pros bank on the big stage

Want to see bank shots at the highest level? The Mosconi Cup runs November 27-30, 2026 at the Caribe Royale Resort in Orlando, Florida, with Team USA taking on Team Europe. Check our Mosconi Cup hub for the latest, and see the pro events calendar for other upcoming events. Broadcast details should be confirmed on Matchroom's official site closer to the event.

Quick recap

  • A bank shot uses a cushion to redirect the ball into a pocket.
  • Angle in is roughly angle out, but speed, spin and table conditions shift it.
  • Aim at the spot on the cushion, not the diamond marker.
  • Test your table, keep a steady medium speed, and change one variable at a time.
  • Bank when it is the best percentage play, not just because it looks cool.

Got a favorite bank-shot story or a spot on your home table that always works? Tell us about it on our Facebook Page. Now go find a rail and give it a try!
